title: Route each acceptance to a layer plane by its keyword cues

facts.note: An acceptance exists that needs a layer plane. The rule applies in any phase and in any artifact or container where an acceptance is routed. Plans, wagons and WMBTs are examples, not required gates.
Detecting that a plane is being assigned or reassigned to an acceptance, new or existing, needs a diff-level or routing-step observer.
Plain term match on the acceptance text. These cues decide the plane, so they are not the only trigger.

fires: A new acceptance criterion is assigned a layer plane.
An existing acceptance is reassigned to a plane, or its plane is re-derived, outside any authoring or revision step (e.g. during routing or re-triage).
An acceptance's wording now has cues for a different plane than the one assigned.
A plane assignment is needed to select the layer sequence (planner.criteria.sequence-routing).
doesNotFire: Implementing code for an acceptance whose plane is already assigned and is not being changed.
Editing prose or docs that contain no acceptance criteria.
Reviewing test code where no acceptance plane assignment is involved.

given: An acceptance criterion is being assigned or reassigned to a layer plane
when: The plane is chosen for that acceptance
then: Choose the plane (presentation, application, domain, integration) that the acceptance's keyword cues indicate in the plane keyword table.
prefer: presentation cues: display, visible, screen, render, animation, button, form, modal.
application cues: workflow, orchestrate, use case, policy, state, saga.
domain cues: rule, validate, aggregate, entity, invariant, business.
integration cues: database, persist, external, queue, api, webhook, repository.
avoid: Assigning a plane that contradicts the acceptance's keyword cues (e.g. putting a 'persist' or 'webhook' acceptance in presentation).
Rewording an acceptance just to hit or avoid a keyword so that a preferred plane gets selected.
why: The keyword-derived plane drives the downstream plane-to-layer-sequence routing. A wrong plane sends the work to the wrong layers.
evidence: Each acceptance's assigned plane matches the plane whose keywords appear in its text.
The plane that sequence routing uses equals the keyword-derived plane.
verifier_detail: Term plane_keywords ('Plane keywords'): layer -> routing keywords.
